mainTopic: Why the משנה says a נזיר shaves for a dead body, what counts as נצל, and whether a poured stream connects vessels
overview: The משנה lists kinds of טומאת מת that make a נזיר shave. The גמרא asks why it needs to say 'for a dead body', since smaller parts already make him shave. רבי יוסי answers that it means a corpse with less than a כזית of flesh. That answer is rejected with a קל וחומר from a limb. The גמרא then gives two better answers: רבי יוחנן's נפל whose limbs are not joined by sinews, and רבא's tiny body whose main frame or most of its bones hold less than a רובע עצמות. Next the גמרא defines נצל as corpse flesh or fluid that melted and then hardened. רבי ירמיה explains that hardening shows it is real corpse fluid and not phlegm or spittle. אביי asks רבה whether נצל applies to an animal, and a proof from melted fat is pushed away. Finally the גמרא quotes a משנה: a poured stream is pure, except for thick honey and batter.

steps.title: רבי יוסי refuses to stay silent
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says that if no one answers, people will say the Torah has no one left to explain it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: People will say, 'מאיר has died, יהודה got angry, יוסי kept quiet.' What will become of the Torah?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short story line that sets up the next move. רבי יוסי decides he must answer the question about the משנה so the Torah is not left unexplained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question 'why does the משנה need to say על המת?' was left hanging. רבי מאיר had died and רבי יהודה was too angry to answer. רבי יוסי feels responsible to speak up, and his answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'lay down'; a gentle way of saying 'died'
Got angry
Kept silent
What will become of the Torah?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
People will say: Meir has died,
Yehuda got angry, Yosei kept silent —
what will become of the Torah?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section by setting up רבי יוסי's answer to the question from before.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone must answer the question so the Torah is not left unexplained.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: a corpse with less than an olive-bulk of flesh
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says the משנה's 'for a dead body' teaches that a נזיר shaves even for a corpse with less than a כזית of flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: The משנה only needed to say it for a corpse that does not have an olive-bulk of flesh on it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי gives his answer: 'for a dead body' teaches a new case, a whole corpse that has less than a כזית of flesh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כזית of corpse flesh is the normal amount that brings טומאה. רבי יוסי says the משנה adds that a whole corpse makes a נזיר shave even if its flesh is less than that amount. So the words 'על המת' are not extra.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed only for... (introduces the special case the text comes to teach)
An olive-bulk, the basic size for corpse flesh to bring טומאה
Flesh

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
It was needed only
phrases.notes: He means the משנה's words 'for a dead body' are needed only for the following case.

phrases.english: for a corpse that does not have an olive-bulk of flesh on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לְמֵת שֶׁאֵין עָלָיו כְּזַיִת בָּשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the answer that רבי יוסי promised to give.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the משנה need to say that a נזיר shaves for a dead body?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: To teach that a whole corpse makes him shave even when it has less than a כזית of flesh.

steps.title: Challenge: a whole corpse is more than a limb
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבי יוסי's answer: if a limb makes him shave, surely a whole corpse does too, so there is nothing new.
steps.simpleTranslation: But one could still say: if he shaves for a limb from it, then for all of it, is it not all the more so?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוסי's answer with a קל וחומר. We would know his case anyway, so the משנה still did not need to say it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already says a נזיר shaves for a limb of a corpse, even with little flesh on it. If part of a body is enough, then a whole body, even with little flesh, is surely enough. So רבי יוסי's case is obvious, and the question returns.

keyTerms.meaning: And still, even so (the problem has not gone away)
A limb
He shaves (the נזיר's shaving after becoming טמא)
Is it not all the more so? (a קל וחומר)

phrases.english: But one could still say:
for a limb from it he shaves,
phrases.notes: This points back to the משנה, which says a נזיר shaves for a limb of a dead body.

phrases.english: for all of it, is it not all the more so?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יוסי's answer from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's claim that 'על המת' teaches a corpse with less than a כזית of flesh
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from a limb: if part of a corpse makes him shave, a whole corpse surely does, so no extra words are needed.

steps.title: Using רבי יוחנן: a fetus without sinews
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the משנה like רבי יוחנן: it is about a נפל whose limbs are not yet joined by sinews.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, as רבי יוחנן said: It was needed only for a miscarried fetus whose limbs were not yet joined by sinews. Here too, it is about a miscarried fetus whose limbs were not joined by sinews.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer, borrowing a rule that רבי יוחנן said somewhere else. 'For a dead body' teaches the case of a very early נפל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נפל whose limbs are not yet joined by sinews has no proper 'limb', so the limb rule cannot teach us about it. A קל וחומר from a limb therefore does not work here. The משנה must say on its own that this whole small body makes a נזיר shave.

keyTerms.meaning: As (so-and-so) said
A miscarried fetus
Were joined, tied together
Sinews
Here too (applying the same idea to our case)

phrases.english: Rather, as Rabbi Yochanan said:
It was needed only for a miscarried fetus
whose limbs were not yet joined by sinews.
Here too:
it is about a miscarried fetus whose limbs were not joined by sinews.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבי יוסי's rejected answer with a case that the קל וחומר cannot cover.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought 'על המת' meant a normal corpse with little flesh, which a limb already teaches.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means a נפל without sinews, where there is no real 'limb' to learn from.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this נפל is not a 'מת'. It is fully a dead body for טומאה. The point is only that it has no proper limbs, so the limb rule cannot teach about it.

steps.title: רבא: most of a tiny skeleton
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers differently: the משנה is about most of the frame or most of the bones of a tiny body that has less than a רובע עצמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It was needed only for the majority of its frame or the majority of its number of bones, which do not contain a quarter-קב of bones.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second, separate answer to why the משנה says 'for a dead body'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually bones bring טומאה through a רובע עצמות (a quarter-קב). A very small body might not have that much, yet most of its frame or most of its bones count like a whole body. Since the part-amount (רובע) is missing, we could not learn this from the parts, so the משנה had to say it.

keyTerms.meaning: Most of its frame (the main structure of the body)
Most of its number (most of the body's bones by count)
A quarter-kav of bones, the usual amount of bones that brings טומאה

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers explain why the משנה says 'for a dead body': רבי יוחנן's נפל without sinews, and רבא's tiny body with less than a רובע עצמות. Both are cases where the smaller-part rules do not help.

phrases.english: Rava said:
It was needed only for the majority of its frame
or the majority of its number of bones,
which do not contain a quarter-kav of bones.
phrases.notes: A קב is a measure of volume. A quarter of it is the usual amount of bones that brings טומאה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לְרוֹב בִּנְיָינוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from the one in step 4 to the same question.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The part-amounts (limb, רובע עצמות) would already teach every case.
steps.terutzMaskana: For a tiny body with less than a רובע, only the whole-body rule makes the נזיר shave.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: what is נצל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה, a כזית of a corpse and a כזית of נצל, and asks what נצל is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: For an olive-bulk of a corpse and for an olive-bulk of נצל. And what is נצל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next phrase in the משנה and sets up a question about the meaning of a word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses the unusual word נצל. Before going on, the גמרא wants to define exactly what it means.

keyTerms.meaning: Decayed fluid of a corpse that has hardened
And which is...? (asks for a definition)

phrases.english: For an olive-bulk of a corpse
and for an olive-bulk of netzel.
And what is netzel?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The definition of the word נצל.

steps.title: נצל defined: congealed flesh and bubbled fluid
steps.stepSummary: נצל is corpse flesh that turned to liquid and then congealed, and corpse fluid that bubbled and hardened.
steps.simpleTranslation: The flesh of the corpse that congealed, and fluid that boiled up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question and defines נצל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נצל is not plain liquid. It is corpse flesh or fluid that melted and then firmed up again. A כזית of this also makes a נזיר shave.

keyTerms.meaning: Congealed, hardened
Fluid that oozes from a corpse
Bubbled up, began to boil

phrases.english: flesh of the corpse that congealed,
and fluid that boiled up.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: נצל is congealed corpse flesh and corpse fluid that bubbled and hardened.

steps.title: When does congealing make any difference?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the role of congealing in the definition of נצל: if we don't know the fluid came from the corpse, congealing shouldn't help; if we do know, it should be impure even without congealing.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we talking about? If we don't know that the fluid came from the dead body, then even if it hardened, so what? And if we do know it came from the dead body, it should be impure even if it did not harden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the definition of נצל from Step 7, which said the fluid must have hardened. It asks what case would make the hardening matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא sets up two options and shows that neither one works. If the source of the fluid is unknown, hardening does not prove it came from the corpse. If the source is known, it should make the נזיר impure right away, so the hardening seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?
If you say (the first option being tested)
Congealed, hardened
His / its own (here: from the corpse)

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If we say that we do not know
that it is from it,
phrases.notes: Literally "that it is his." He means the fluid came from the dead body.

phrases.english: when it congealed, what of it?
Rather, we know that it is from it,
then even though it did not congeal, it should be impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the requirement of congealing given in the definition of נצל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The detail in Step 7 that corpse fluid must have congealed to count as נצל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dilemma: whether the source is unknown or known, congealing seems not to change the law.

steps.title: Congealing tells us what kind of fluid it is
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה explains that the case is fluid that surely came from the body but is of an unknown type. Hardening shows it is corpse fluid; not hardening means it may be phlegm or spittle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: We are dealing with an unclear case. If it hardened, it is corpse fluid. If it did not harden, maybe it is just his phlegm or spittle.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers the challenge by finding a third case. The fluid surely came from the body, but we don't know what kind of fluid it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed there were only two cases: unknown source or known source. רבי ירמיה adds a middle case: the source is known, but the type of fluid is not. Hardening is the test that tells impure corpse fluid apart from phlegm and spittle, which do not make a person impure.

keyTerms.meaning: In an unspecified, unclear case
Fluid that comes out of a corpse
His phlegm
His spittle

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said: It is about an unspecified case.
phrases.notes: The fluid came from the body, but we don't know which kind of fluid it is.

phrases.english: If it congealed, it is corpse fluid;
if it did not congeal,
perhaps it is his phlegm and his spittle.

steps.whatToRemember: Hardening is a test of what kind of fluid it is. It shows that fluid from the body is real corpse fluid and not phlegm or spittle.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma of Step 8 by finding a third case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finding a middle case (the source is known, the type of fluid is not)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The only choices were an unknown source or a fully known corpse fluid, so congealing seemed pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: Congealing tells real corpse fluid apart from harmless body fluids like phlegm and spittle.

steps.title: Does נצל apply to an animal carcass?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רבה whether the law of נצל, melted and hardened flesh, also applies to an animal, or only to a human corpse.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי asked רבה: Is there נצל for an animal, or not? Do we say the tradition only taught נצל that comes from a person, and not from an animal? Or perhaps there is no difference?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. אביי asks whether fluid from a dead animal carcass makes things impure the way נצל from a human corpse does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law of נצל is a tradition (גמירי). The question is how far that tradition reaches. Maybe it was only taught for a human corpse. Or maybe melted flesh is always treated like the flesh itself, so the same law applies to a נבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked of him (a formal question)
Flesh that melted into liquid and then hardened
An animal
We have it as a tradition
There is no difference

phrases.english: Abaye asked of Rabba:
Is there נצל for an animal,
or is there no נצל for an animal?
Do we say that we have a tradition
about נצל that comes from a person,
but that which comes from an animal, not?
Or perhaps there is no difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the definition of נצל and asks whether it also covers animals.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether melted and hardened flesh of a נבלה makes things impure like human נצל.

steps.title: According to one view, the question is easy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that according to the opinion that a נבלה gives severe impurity only while fit for a person and light impurity only while fit for a dog, the question is easily answered.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to the one who says: severe impurity lasts until it is unfit for a stranger, and light impurity lasts until it is unfit for a dog. By that view, it is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to work on אביי's question. It says that by one opinion the answer is simple, which sets up a question about the other opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By this opinion, a נבלה gives severe impurity only while a person could still eat it. Melted flesh is no longer fit for people, so animal נצל would not carry that severe impurity. The real question remains for the opinion that does not hold this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well according to the one who says
Severe impurity (passed on by touching and carrying)
Light impurity (makes food impure)
Fine, it works out well

steps.confusionAlert: This is only half of an argument. The words "הניחא למאן דאמר" mean "this is fine by one opinion." Expect the גמרא to ask next about the other opinion.

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says
severe impurity lasts until it is unfit for a stranger,
phrases.notes: Meaning the נבלה gives severe impurity only as long as a person could still eat it.

phrases.english: and light impurity lasts until it is unfit for a dog —
it is well.
phrases.notes: By this view, melted flesh is no longer fit for people, so animal נצל would not carry severe impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר טוּמְאָה חֲמוּרָה עַד לְגֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins to answer אביי's question by showing it is simple according to one opinion.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to the opinion that severe impurity lasts only while the meat is fit for people, animal נצל does not carry severe impurity, since melted flesh is not fit for people.

steps.title: What about the opinion that impurity lasts until it is unfit for a dog?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the question is still open for the opinion that a נבלה keeps its severe impurity as long as a dog would eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who says a נבלה has severe impurity until it is unfit even for a dog, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back אביי's question for a second opinion, where the easy answer from step 11 does not work. This sets up the next move: a source that might answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the first opinion, melted flesh is no longer fit for people, so it obviously loses its severe impurity. Under this second opinion, impurity lasts as long as a dog would eat it. Melted animal flesh may still be fit for a dog, so the question of נצל in an animal comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: according to the one who says
severe impurity (the full impurity of a נבלה)
until it is unfit for a dog
what is there to say?

phrases.english: But according to the one who says
severe impurity lasts until [it is unfit] for a dog
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר טוּמְאָה חֲמוּרָה עַד לְכֶלֶב, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 11 answered the question for one opinion. This step reopens it for the other opinion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Under the 'until unfit for a dog' opinion, does נצל apply to a dead animal?

steps.title: Proof from fat melted in fire versus in the sun
steps.stepSummary: A source rules that fat melted in fire is impure and fat melted in the sun is pure. If impurity lasted until it was unfit for a dog, sun-melted fat should also be impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if they melted it in fire, it is impure; if in the sun, it is pure. And if you think impurity lasts until it is unfit for a dog, even when melted in the sun it should also be impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to try to answer the question from step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sun-melted fat tastes bad to people, but a dog would still eat it. The source says it is pure anyway. This suggests that melted animal matter loses its impurity even under the 'dog' opinion, so נצל would not apply to an animal.

keyTerms.meaning: they melted it
fire
the sun
and if it enters your mind (if you think)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
if they melted it in fire, it is impure
phrases.notes: The 'it' here is the fat of a dead animal (נבלה).

phrases.english: in the sun, it is pure.
And if you think [impurity lasts] until [it is unfit] for a dog,
even [melted] in the sun, [it should] also [be impure]!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question raised in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That melted animal matter, like נצל, does not stay impure even under the 'until unfit for a dog' opinion.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A תוספתא ruling: fat melted in fire is impure, but fat melted in the sun is pure.

steps.title: Sun-melted fat had already rotted into dust
steps.stepSummary: Fat only melts in the sun after it has rotted. Rotten fat is like dust, so it is pure for that reason, and the source proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does it melt in the sun? After it has rotted. Once it has rotted, it is like dust.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fat is left out in the sun only after it has already gone bad. Rotted fat is not even fit for a dog; it counts as dust. So it is pure because it rotted, not because it melted. The source tells us nothing about נצל in an animal.

keyTerms.meaning: when?
it rotted / went bad
dust (no longer counts as food)

steps.confusionAlert: The sun is not what makes the fat pure. The rotting that happened first is what made it pure.

phrases.english: When does it melt?
after it has rotted, [it melts] in the sun.
Once it has rotted,
it has become [like] dust.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. The question about נצל in an animal stays open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The source's case is fat that already rotted into dust, so its purity has nothing to do with melting.
steps.whatToRemember: Under the 'unfit for a dog' opinion, the question of נצל in a dead animal is left without proof here.

steps.title: New topic: anything poured is pure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a related topic by quoting a משנה: anything poured is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: anything poured is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new related discussion by quoting a משנה about a poured stream of liquid. This sets up the analysis that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A stream of liquid poured from a pure vessel into an impure one does not count as connecting them. So the impurity of the lower vessel does not travel up the stream to the upper one.

keyTerms.meaning: a poured stream of liquid
ritually pure

phrases.english: We learned [in a משנה]:
Anything poured is pure.
phrases.notes: מכשירין 5:9. The stream does not link a pure upper vessel to an impure lower one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the נצל question and opens a related topic about poured liquids.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A poured stream of liquid does not connect two vessels for impurity, so the upper vessel stays pure.

steps.title: Thick honey and batter are the exception
steps.stepSummary: The משנה limits its rule: a poured stream is pure, except for very thick honey (דבש הזיפים) and batter (צפיחית), which do connect the vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: Except for very thick honey and batter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the quote of the משנה from step 15 by adding its exception. Thick honey and batter poured into an impure vessel do make the upper vessel impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic rule is that a thin stream does not join the upper liquid to the impure liquid below, so the upper part stays pure. Thick honey and batter are different because they are so heavy and sticky that they act like one solid piece. Since they count as one piece, the stream works as a חיבור (connection) and the impurity reaches up.

keyTerms.meaning: Except for
A very thick kind of honey
Batter, such as flour mixed with honey
A connection that joins two things for טומאה

steps.whatToRemember: A poured stream is pure because it does not connect the vessels. Thick, sticky foods like דבש הזיפים and צפיחית are the exception, because they hold together as one piece.
steps.confusionAlert: This exception is not saying that honey and batter are a special kind of liquid that carries impurity better. The point is that they are so thick they are treated like one solid piece, so the stream does connect.

phrases.english: Except for very thick honey
phrases.notes: This finishes the rule from step 15, that anything poured is pure.

phrases.english: and batter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה quoted in step 15 by stating the exception to its general rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A poured stream does not link vessels for טומאה, except thick honey and batter, which do link them because they hold together as one piece.
